title: What Is AI
summary: AI is a helpful tool — you input a request and get a response — it's not magic.

sections.heading: Orientation
sections.subtitle: What Will You Understand?
sections.contentMarkdown:
- What Will You Understand? AI (artificial intelligence) is not magic — it’s a tool that takes a request from you and gives a response. Like a smart assistant on your phone.
- Why Now? Everyone is talking about AI, and it’s natural to feel that the topic is big. This lesson breaks it down for you in simple steps without complications.
- What After the Lesson? You will try one AI tool in a small part of your day — and you will feel confident that you can complete the rest of the path.

sections.heading: Tension
sections.subtitle: A Familiar Situation
sections.contentMarkdown: Do you hear a lot about AI but don’t know where to start? That’s normal. Some people say, "Use ChatGPT" without explaining what it is. You don’t need to be an expert today. You just need to understand the basic idea and try it once yourself. If you feel overwhelmed, take it step by step — each small section on its own.

sections.heading: Core Idea
sections.subtitle: The Basic Idea
sections.contentMarkdown:
AI is a helpful tool — it’s not magic and not a replacement for you - AI is a program that learns from many examples and gives you a response close to what you requested. Like a calculator: it saves time, but the decision is yours.
- It doesn’t think like a human — it calculates the best response based on what it has seen before. So it makes mistakes sometimes, and that’s normal.
- What matters is not understanding all the technical details — but to open any tool and try a simple request. Experimenting teaches you faster than any long explanation.

sections.heading: Glossary
sections.subtitle: Key Terms
sections.contentMarkdown:
| Term | Meaning | Example |
|---------|--------|------|
| AI (artificial intelligence) | A program that helps you with a specific task — writing, summarizing, organizing ideas | When you ask ChatGPT to write a message — that’s using AI |
| Model | The name of the ready program you chat with | ChatGPT, Gemini, and Claude — each is a different model, but the idea is the same |

sections.heading: Comparison
sections.subtitle: A Real-Life Example
sections.contentMarkdown:
| If You Misunderstand It | If You Understand It |
|--------------|-------------|
| You expect it to understand your intent the first time, and you get frustrated when the response is not appropriate. So you leave and say, "It doesn’t work for me" | You write a clear request, see the response, and adjust your question. Each attempt teaches you how to interact with it as a tool — not as a human |

sections.heading: Mission
sections.subtitle: Your Mission
sections.contentMarkdown:
Introduction: Try AI in a simple part of your day. Open any free AI (ChatGPT, Gemini, or Claude), ask for something small, and write what happened. If you don’t have an account now: write the request you would send + the tool you would open — that’s acceptable. Delivery:
1. What did you ask the AI? (or what would you have asked?)
2. Which tool did you use or will you use?
3. What was the response — in one or two lines (or "I will try later")
4. What surprised you in the experience? Evaluation Criteria: | Dimension | Weight | Criteria |
|-------|-------|---------|
| You Tried It Yourself | 70% | A clear request sent to AI and you saw a response — or a planned attempt (the request + the tool) |
| Your Observation | 30% | You wrote something simple about your experience — even if the response was not perfect |
